html:
The Constitution of Tonga was granted by George Tupou I in 1875. It is one of the oldest written constitutions still in force in the world, and the base of the modern state of Tonga.

It set up a king, a privy council and a parliament with seats for nobles and for commoners, and laid down a bill of rights. All land belongs to the crown and nobles, and land laws promised every Tongan man a plot to farm; land cannot be sold to foreigners.

These rules helped Tonga stay independent, as a British protected state from 1900 to 1970 but never a colony. Reforms after the 2006 riots gave elected commoners a majority in parliament from 2010.
